metric.metric: Temperature and humidity, hot and cold aisle
metric.target: ASHRAE's recommended envelope for most IT equipment classes is roughly 18 to 27 degrees C inlet.
metric.definition: Continuous inlet-air temperature and relative humidity at the rack face, monitored separately for cold aisles that feed equipment and hot aisles that exhaust it.

reading.body:
Temperature and humidity, tracked separately for hot and cold aisles, measure continuous inlet-air temperature and relative humidity at the rack face, with ASHRAE's Technical Committee 9.9 setting a recommended envelope of roughly 18 to 27 degrees Celsius inlet temperature for most IT equipment classes.

Sustained inlet temperatures above that spec force processors to throttle before they fail, which means the symptom of bad cooling is slower compute long before it becomes dead compute, a gradual and easily missed degradation rather than a sudden outage. Humidity outside the recommended range carries its own separate risk, static discharge when air is too dry and condensation when it is too wet.

This metric groups with airflow and static pressure and liquid coolant temperature and flow rate under Cooling and climate, three measurements that together describe whether a facility's cooling system is actually delivering the thermal environment its equipment needs, rather than simply having enough rated cooling capacity on paper.
